rows: Trees down on West Walker Street near Victory Lakes Subdivision.

Semi-tractor trailer overturned onto another vehicle on Interstate 45 at FM 646. Winds also blew down a few large concrete wall structures at a construction site at the same intersection. Numerous fences and store signs were also blown down in and around League City and Dickinson…
Tree down near the intersection of Deats Road and Highway 3.
Utility pole and power lines downed.
Thunderstorm moved over west Galveston Island.
An EF-0 tornado blew out garage doors and tossed around some port covers on Tiki Island.

An EF-0 tornado completely destroyed one mobile home roof and partially damaged another one. There was one minor injury in one of the mobile homes. Trees were also uprooted and one tree fell on a vehicle.
An EF-0 tornado lifted up and spun a sheriff's patrol vehicle. There was also damage to a boat storage unit.
Tree down on one home with numerous downed tree limbs. National Weather Service in League City estimated wind gusts between 50 and 60 mph during the height of the storm.
Wind gust estimated in southeast Dickinson.
Tree downed in the Gulf Village subdivision near Stewart Road.
Tree down on a house and power line near Highway 96 and Interstate 45.

Tornado spotted on the island side of the Causeway Bridge, near Interstate 45 and Teichman Point, moving east to southeast. Damage included a few uprooted trees, various fences, and minor structural damage to a car dealership and motel.
An EF-0 tornado produced minor damage to a small home and garage. There was also minor shingle damage to a residence across the street.
Large tree downed on a car in Clear Lake Shores.
Tornado was spotted from 1700 Main Street in La Marque.
Nickel size hail was reported in the town of Santa Fe.
Penny size hail was observed at the intersection of FM 517 and SH 146.
A severe thunderstorm produced penny size hail.
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail.
Large trees were downed in the Clear Lake Forest subdivision.

The tornado touched down in a marshy area a few miles south southeast of Hitchcock as reported by several witnesses and captured on video. The damage path extended into the Harborwalk community with damage to several homes. Six garage doors were damaged or destroyed. A large wood…
Severe wind gust measured at Eagle Point PORTS buoy.

The tornado began as a waterspout moved onto the beach near 29th Street and Seawall Blvd. A police cruiser had its windows blown out and the roof of a souvenir shop at 29th and Seawall was blown off. Further inland, a house on stilts was blown over and the roof of a mobile home w…
Wind gust was measured at Galveston Scholes Field.
A tornado touched down at a industrial plant. It knocked over 10 empty trailers and did minor damage to plant.
A severe thunderstorm downed a tree along Cemetery Road in Santa Fe.

A severe thunderstorm produced straight line wind damage in the Westwood Circle area of La Marque. The winds downed some fences and uprooted a few trees. This storm produced a tornado in the Mall of the Mainland area just a few minutes later.

This EF-0 tornado was observed by a police officer to touch down in the Mall of the Mainland parking lot. Tree limbs were downed and some shallow rooted trees were knocked over. A combination of tornadic winds and heavy rainfall likely contributed to some Mall roof damage. Anothe…
Quarter sized hail reported near the intersection of FM 518 and FM 528.
Quarter sized hail reported along Highway 6 from the intersection with FM 2004 east to the fire and police stations in Hitchcock.
Golfball sized hail reported at the public works department building.
A wind gust of 78 mph was recorded at Moody Gardens.
Windshields damaged and power outages caused in La Marque.
Numerous power lines downed on the island from communities on the West End eastward into downtown Galveston.
There was wind damage to commercial building windows and minor roof damage to the fire station. One residence was damaged by a vehicle that was pivoted around and struck the home.

A severe thunderstorms produced baseball to softball sized hail in Hitchcock. The central and western parts of the town received extreme damage to vehicles and home roofs and windows. There was also significant damage to the Midway Church, a fire station, and in two trailer parks…
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail.
A severe thunderstorm produced ping pong to tennis ball sized hail near Sante Fe.
A severe thunderstorm produced golf ball sized hail that damaged vehicles near Jamaica Beach.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew down a utility pole and power lines in Galveston.
A tornado destroyed a storage trailer and knocked down a fence near the intersection of Highland Bayou Drive and Mallard Street. There was one injury.
An EF0 tornado briefly touched down at an oil refinery. There was minimal damage to one of the buildings, and one vehicle's window was shattered.
Dime sized hail was observed in the Westover Park subdivision of League City.
Thunderstorm winds blew a roof off a home.
Golf ball sized hail was reported close to the intersection of Heards Lane and 68th Street on Galveston Island.

Penny sized hail occurred to the northwest of La Marque.
The quarter size hail was reported in Friendswood.
The dime size hail was reported in League City.

Quarter size hail was reported near the intersection of 67th Street and Heards Lane.
A waterspout moved onshore and became a weak tornado just east of the Galveston Fishing Pier at 61st Street. The tornado moved across Seawall Boulevard and dissipated. There was no damage.
Six power poles were blown down near the intersection of Highway 87 and Helen Blvd.
A couple of trees were downed (one on a house) along Avenue I between 21st Street and 24th Street.
Power poles were snapped at Crenshaw Elementary School.
An EF0 tornado damaged a Holiday Inn along Termini-San Luis Pass Road. Damage included blown out windows and lattice damage. Witnesses indicated this was a waterspout that moved onshore.
Funnel cloud sighting with fence damage near Ferry Road.
Trees down, minor roof damage in Bacliff. Fences down.
An EF0 tornado downed trees and branches along either side of Benson's Bayou. Damage included home and vehicle windows along with residential fences.
Damage was reported near the intersection of FM 646 and Highway 3.
There was some minor residential awning and tree limb damage.
An oleander tree was knocked down and a wooden bench swing collapsed around the intersection of 15th Street and Avenue M.
A power pole was downed near an apartment complex on 21st Street.
Numerous trees were downed off of Gordy Road.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor structure damage. Winds rolled over an exposed, non-anchored mobile trailer off of Dike Drive.
Thunderstorm winds downed two palm trees on Harborside Drive and 29th Street.
There was a report of a collapsed residence on Ave S and 47th street.
Trees and fences were downed and there were damaged and destroyed trampolines, gazebos, barn roofs and retail signs.
There were various reports of pea to nickel sized hail.
Some travel trailers were flipped over.
Brief touchdown. Peeled off tin roof, damaged manufactured home and storage shed.
There were reports of trees and power lines downed along Highway 96 just west of Highway 3.
Thunderstorm winds damaged the roof of the volunteer fire department.
A large area of the Bolivar Peninsula was without power after strong thunderstorm wind gusts were observed.
There was some roof damage to a Texas City business.
Large tree limbs and some fencing were blown down.
The wind gust was measured at KGLS.
Dime sized hail was observed in Texas City.
Severe hail (1 in.) was observed by a member of the public as a squall line moved through Galveston County.

Severe hail (1 in.) was observed by a member of the public as a squall line moved through Galveston County.
Local emergency managers reported a travel trailer knocked over by strong thunderstorm wind gusts.
A waterspout moved onshore. This EF0 tornado lasted a short time and caused no damage.

A palm tree was downed on Texas Clipper Road.
A 64 mph wind gust was recorded at Scholes Field in Galveston at the KGLS ASOS site as a strong thunderstorm moved through the area.
Wind gust was measured at the Galveston ASOS site (KGLS).
Spotty roof, tree and fence damage spotted around Friendswood.
Spotty roof, tree and fence damage spotted around Friendswood.
Quarter sized hail was observed on Galveston Island at the intersection of 20th and Market Streets.
A large tree limb was downed.
Trees were downed near Windsong Intermediate School.
Quarter sized hail was reported along 40th Street East.
Quarter sized hail was reported near the FM 270 and FM 518 intersection.
Wind gust occurred at the Brigantine Cay Court mesonet site.
Wind gust occurred at the Crab Lake WeatherFlow site.
Wind gust occurred at the Crab Lake WeatherFlow site.
A large tree was knocked down onto a road and a parked car.
A social media user documented widespread hail in Gilchrist. The maximum hail diameter observed was 1.25 inches.
Numerous power lines were downed, poles were snapped, trees were downed and there was damage to structures in and around the Dickinson area intersection of Hill Avenue and Salvato Street.
The wind gust occurred at a weather station.
Trees were downed in the League City area just north of FM 518 near Clear Creek.
Measured gust from anemometer on radio tower at Dickinson PD. 25 to 30 feet AGL.
Multiple trees were downed along FM 517 in the area around Dickinson High School. Siding was also ripped of a nearby apartment building.
There was some wind damage across parts of San Leon and Bacliff.
Shingles were blown off and one-inch tree limbs were broken.
Hen egg size hail was observed.
Quarter sized hail was observed at the intersection of FM 646 and FM 517. Report came from a Spaceflight Meteorology Group (SMG) meteorologist.
Golf ball sized hail was observed in the League City area.
Half dollar to hen egg sized hail was observed.
Hail up to baseball sized was collected around the WFO HGX office.
Wind gust occurred at the Avenue N Tempest Weather System site.
Wind gust occurred at the Avenue N Tempest Weather System site.

A member of the public measured a wind gust around 66 MPH near the intersection of 40th Street and Texas Avenue, associated with a thunderstorm that produced a tornado in Galveston county.

A member of the public reported that a tree was blown down near Friendswood.
Galveston county dispatch relayed a report of roof damage to a home around the Bayou Vista area. Wind speeds were estimated to be around 60 mph.
